feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and technical breadth.  
- Strong relevance for digital strategy roles: web/CMS, analytics, governance, multimedia, and cross-channel communications are all well evidenced.  
- Credibility is high due to specific platforms and scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, GA4/BigQuery/Drupal).

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results, not just responsibilities: include measurable outcomes for newsletters, social growth, engagement, conversion, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and avoid repetition.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without it); “content operations and enterprise web improvement” reads awkwardly—consider “content operations, and enterprise web improvements.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two more concrete differentiators, and less repetition of skills already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Replace generic phrases like “expert in” and “strong background” with sharper, evidence-backed positioning tied to enterprise web, governance, analytics, and advocacy communications.
- Emphasize seniority and scope: cross-channel leadership, platform modernization, and systems/workflow design for complex membership or mission-driven organizations.
- Possible rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, analytics, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, editorial governance, and workflow design. Experienced in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, audience-focused content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “workflow/systems” repeat heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” also appears throughout the NACo experience, so keep it brief here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/technical strengths will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance & workflow design,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Group related items to improve scanability and reduce repetition: strategy, platforms, operations, analytics, stakeholder communication, multimedia.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing broad functions (“communication”) with specific tasks (“administration”).
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Workflow systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy messaging • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” and “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeat the header and Soft Skills.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills/Technical + IT, especially web/CMS, analytics, workflow systems, and multimedia.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles by emphasizing advisory scope, platform modernization, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and cross-channel governance as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 outcome-oriented points; e.g., combine digital systems/workflows/analytics with governance/usability/operations.
- Rephrase technical execution bullet to show business value: “Built and optimized Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsites, and member toolkits to support advocacy and storytelling initiatives.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy gains, engagement lifts, or reduced publishing friction.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics” overlaps with the Director role’s analytics/governance bullets.
- Microsite and AI-search language duplicates Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and reserve specifics for the project section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational leadership, and the biggest transformation wins without repeating themes covered in the consultant and prior NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one outcome-led line: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel impact more measurable: add email open/click growth, social engagement/follower growth, video output, or cost/time savings from the in-house studio if available.
- Tighten ops/analytics language: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery; formalized governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Recurring multimedia content/video as a channel” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; focus here on scaling/building the studio and enterprise ownership.
- Governance/workflow language also appears in the current consultant role; keep this entry centered on execution and organizational impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving coordination for editorial and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: managed 4 weekly newsletters; launched/grew weekly advocacy video update; coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams; standardized publishing workflows.
- Replace soft verbs like “helped scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” with direct action verbs: “managed,” “expanded,” “established,” “standardized,” “coordinated.”
- Add metrics if available: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, publishing volume, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; emphasize expansion/operationalization here, not creation.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

- Audience-focused content planning

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:

- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is already covered by recent work experience overseeing web, email, social, and video.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to enterprise web modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first; lead with strategic execution, then key platforms.
- Tighten wording and group related items for readability, e.g.:
- Enterprise CMS modernization (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- Airtable-based operational systems
- AI-enabled search and content discovery experiences
- If space allows, swap “Airtable systems” for “structured content and operational systems” to sound more senior and less tool-specific.
- Consider adding one impact cue if format permits: “for high-volume public-sector sites” or “supporting enterprise publishing operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep this version high-level and save full tool inventory for that section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Microsoft Clarity

- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads more like a tool list than a value statement. Make it sharper, outcome-oriented, and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” style wording is stronger than a pure platform list.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than separating every tool with equal weight.
- Replace generic phrases with business impact language: use “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” and “performance and search optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) - KPI framework development - Executive and leadership dashboarding - SEO, content performance and user behavior analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory below.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it sharper, more senior, and tied to the most recent/credible capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera systems • Virtual event production”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to the most recent roles, this item should signal depth and recency rather than repeat a generic skills list.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider leading with emphasis: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add one short qualifier tied to recent impact, e.g. “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views)” to make the skill credible and outcome-linked.
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS Platforms” for concision and cleaner scanning.
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation detail for the coding/technical line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same CMS tools plus modernization.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere; cut it if space is tight.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, emphasize implementation scope and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and seniority: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping versioned basics (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed for ATS; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “Drupal front-end implementation,” “analytics instrumentation,” or “workflow/deployment automation.”
- Order by impact/recency: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, then front-end languages.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may also overlap with analytics/tooling; consider moving it under Data, Analytics & Optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads like a generic software list. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills, so it should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Split automation tools from collaboration/project tools to sharpen the signal.
- Lead with systems tied to your recent impact: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier” first.
- Rename to something more specific, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”  
  Optional: move “Basecamp” and “Trello” off if they were not used recently or at meaningful scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases elsewhere.
- Slack and Teams are generic workplace tools; keep only if they support a broader systems/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare and undersells a clear strength shown throughout the CV: enterprise email operations and member communications. It should signal scale/use case, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize function and seniority: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms** or **Email, CRM & Member Engagement**.
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** is fine if Dynamics is current; otherwise put the most-used platform first.
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (CRM/email journeys) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**.
- Keep it concise; avoid adding “newsletters” or audience scale here since that impact is stronger in recent NACo experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work experience references to email newsletters and digital channels; keep this as platforms only, not responsibilities.
- “Engagement” may feel vague unless paired with CRM/member context.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any metrics you can add.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Split into concrete outcomes: website refresh support, livestream/video production, workflow improvements, and informal supervision/mentoring.
- Add measurable detail where possible: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social volume supported, or size/timing of the website refresh.
- Suggested version: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, improved day-to-day workflows across web, email, social and multimedia, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates. Also provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows” also appears in later roles; frame this as early process-building rather than organization-wide leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generically and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a stronger second clause: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a specific support function only if true (e.g., “produced digital and multimedia content for program communications”).
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audiences served, or types of stakeholders/programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid over-claiming broad digital leadership here; keep this focused on innovation/research coordination plus the first podcast launch.
